Occurrences.Kwic: 僧遂作一圓相，師便打曰：這漆桶，碌甎也不識。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120) (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): Fachang Yiyu strikes and says “this lacquer bucket” in his own section.

Occurrences.Kwic: 作玄妙提撕領略老和尚云若是天寧則不然或有人問只對他道薰風自南來殿閣生微凉只念這兩句詩此是唐柳公權與文宗聯句自家忽然在這一聯詩上打破漆桶當時如貧得寶如暗得燈如病得醫如子得母平生千疑萬慮如一把亂絲將利刀一截截斷從前許多無明煩惱一時斷了當下寂滅如斬一綟絲一斬一切斬證法時亦然一證一切證一了一切了一悟一切悟更無前
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (M/M59/M59n1540.xml). General Discourses of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師普說): In his own discourse, Dahui Zonggao says that while reciting the paired verse he suddenly ‘broke open the lacquer bucket’ (打破漆桶).

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：這漆桶前後觸忤多少賢良！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X81/X81n1568.xml). Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (Vols. 10–25) (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)): Sansheng Huiran strikes with his sitting cloth and calls the head monk a lacquer bucket that has offended many worthies.

Senses.Explanation: A black-lacquer bucket is a blunt address for someone presented as unable to distinguish what is directly before them. Teachers apply it after failed recognitions, circular signs, or answers, and later commentators repeat it as an encounter verdict.
